segments.text: At the end of the 18th century, France was suffering from a serious financial crisis and famine.
Heavy taxes weighed on peasants and the urban poor
While the gap between ordinary people and the royal court of Louis XVI's
And Marie Antoinette at Versailles was simply too great
The thought of the Enlightenment philosophers Voltaire and Rousseau
Had already spread among the educated class
Liberty, equality, and the dignity of the human person
These ideals would become the trigger of the revolution
On July 14, 1789
The citizens of Paris stormed the Bastille prison
This became the starting point of the French Revolution
In August of the same year, the National Assembly adopted the Declaration of the Rights of Man
And declared that all people held equal rights
In 1793, Louis XVI was executed by the guillotine
France was transformed from a monarchy into a republic
But in the middle of the revolution, the Jacobins under Rotspier
Carried out the reign of terror
And tens of thousands were executed as enemies
In 1799, the young soldier Napoleon Bonaparte took power in a coup
And the chaos of the revolution came to an end
He would become emperor in 1804
But the reform that the revolution brought
Equality before the law
Freedom of religion
The protection of private property
Spread throughout Europe
Liberty, equality, fraternity
The three ideals of the French Revolution still flow
At the foundation of every democratic society
In the world today
